messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE -> high token accounting spike for tenant HelixHealth in vpc-prod-12 (dedicated pool). 3.7M tokens ingested in last 15m, billing alert threshold breached. Paging oncall.

irene (oncall): acked. i'm pulling logs and token samples now. curious if this is a true usage burst or a tokenizer/encoding issue.

alex: seeing lots of requests with very large encoded lengths from 10.8.1.23 -> their proxy. sample request_id=af3c1b. raw prompt length ~ 45k chars, tokenized -> ~86k tokens. that's not normal for typical HelixHealth workloads. attaching snippet.

alex: ```
REQUEST (truncated):
{"patient_note":"\u0048\u0065\u006c\u006c\u006f ...\u00e9\u00f1 ... (lots of escaped sequences)"}
Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-16
```

samir: looks like double-encoding / UTF-16 BOM -> our tokenizer is counting every 2 bytes as separate codepoints in some pre-tokenization step. i've reproduced locally: feed the same UTF-16 JSON string into tokenizer -> token count ~2x expected. when decoded to UTF-8 first, token count drops to expected ~42k.

mel (cust-eng): contacted Helix ops (via DM and email). they've reported a recent middleware patch that changed how they serialize notes (from UTF-8 to surrogate-pair-heavy UTF-16 for Windows clients). they believe it was to fix an internal search bug.

irene (oncall): immediate mitigations we can apply: 1) per-tenant max_tokens cap on the VPC gateway (enforce 30k) 2) temporary billing throttle / soft-deny for requests > 40k tokens 3) add automatic decoding step in the VPC ingress that normalizes to UTF-8 before tokenization. which can we do fast?

ops-bot: scheduled job created: vpc-prod-12 -> apply-request-size-cap(tenant=HelixHealth, cap_tokens=30000) in 60s.

alex: I can push the gateway patch to normalize encoding (small change in nginx lua plugin) — rolling patch would take ~12 min to deploy to all nodes, can do immediate canary to 2 pods. sample patch below.

alex: ```lua
-- ingress normalization snippet
local body = ngx.req.get_body_data()
if body then
  -- try to detect UTF-16 BOM and decode
  if body:sub(1,2) == "\\255\\254" or body:sub(1,2) == "\\254\\255" then
    body = util.utf16_to_utf8(body)
  end
  ngx.req.init_body( length )
  ngx.req.set_body_data(body)
end
```

samir: canary sounds good. also adding a short-term policy in the runtime: if tokenized_count > 50k then downgrade to a cheaper model (gpt-small) and tag for billing review so customer isn't charged full price until resolved. that buys us headroom.

mel (cust-eng): HelixOps oncall says they'll rollback the middleware change if we need them to; they're trying to avoid rollback during business hours. asked for ETA on a targeted rollback by EOD.

irene (oncall): ok plan: 1) apply gateway cap (ops-bot scheduled) 2) canary deploy encoding-normalize patch to 2 pods now (alex) 3) runtime fallback rule for huge token requests -> gpt-small (samir) 4) send customer-facing note about investigation and temporary rate limiting (mel) 5) collect token samples and billing delta for postmortem.

ops-bot: job started: canary deploy patch to vpc-prod-12/gateway-pod-03.

alex: canary deployed to pod-03. logs show incoming request now decoded to UTF-8 and tokens halved for same payload. example: request_id=af3c1b tokenized before=86300 after=42850.

irene (oncall): applying runtime rule now: ```rb
# runtime routing rule
if token_count > 50000 and tenant == 'HelixHealth' then route_to = 'gpt-small-fallback' tag = 'enc-mismatch-protect' end
```
rule applied in 45s.

samir: adding billing_exempt tag to requests flagged as encoding-mismatch so we can credit if needed. implemented a ledger entry for audit.

mel (cust-eng): message sent to HelixHealth ops: "We've identified a tokenizer/encoding mismatch triggered by a recent middleware change. We've applied temporary protections (request-size cap, model fallback) to limit cost impact while we and your team work on a rollback or encoding normalization. We'll share a mitigation timeline and billing impact shortly." they replied: "appreciate it. we'll push a targeted rollback to the patch tomorrow morning if urgent."

jude (night-oncall): i'm taking handoff at 18:00 UTC. leaving note: watch for spikes reappearing post-canary rollout; if requests >80% of cap continue -> escalate to infra lead.

irene (oncall): handoff: handing to @jude at 18:00 UTC. summary: token inflation due to UTF-16 serialization in Helix middleware; gateway cap and canary normalization deployed; runtime fallback and billing tags in place. estimated recovery: partial (requests normalized) immediate; full recovery when Helix rolls back their patch or we implement global normalization (~24-36h).

helix_ops_contact: thanks all. we'll prioritize rollback tonight. please share any token samples you need.

ops-bot: metric alert suppressed for tenant HelixHealth for next 2h while mitigations settle.

alex: we should follow up with a runbook entry: "tenant-encoding-spike" that lists triage steps, quickpatch snippet (above), and billing review checklist. assigning to samir + irene.

samir: will draft runbook and a billing reconciliation spreadsheet. will flag for finance to review any credits.

irene (oncall): closing page for now but leaving thread open. will update after Helix rollback or tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:
